summary: Reproduced and verified fix for the reported bug: when the Gemini provider is selected with an INVALID key, the client must automatically fall back to the Serveur provider. Test used a fake key 'AIzaFAKE_BIDON_KEY_FOR_FALLBACK_TEST_...' in Réglages → provider-gemini, then activated Mode Candidat and sent 'Parlez-moi de vous.' via message-input. Gemini returned HTTP 400 (visible in console: 'Failed to load resource: 400'), streamMessage's try/catch caught the error and, because no delta had been emitted (`emitted=false`), invoked `onFallback` (toast 'Gemini indisponible — bascule automatique sur le mode Serveur') then re-streamed through streamServer against /api/generate. A full COPILOTE (CANDIDAT-mode) answer was produced end-to-end; mode-badge stayed CANDIDAT and message thread ended with 2 messages (user + assistant).
critical_code_review_comments: Fallback logic in api.js streamMessage lines 244-263 is correct: it only falls back if `emitted===false` and error is not AbortError. Good defensive design — once tokens have started to stream from Gemini, a mid-stream error will NOT restart on the server (would double-stream). This is the right trade-off.
streamGemini surfaces detailed error via `Gemini 400 — API key not valid...` which is helpful in the toast fallback message.

Minor: onFallback toast auto-dismisses in ~4s; a user who blinks may not see it. Consider making it slightly longer (6s) or persistent until first delta arrives so users understand the switch happened.
seed_data_creation: One fresh session created via UI (localStorage cleared before test).
context_for_next_testing_agent: To retest this fallback: clear localStorage, open Réglages, click provider-gemini, put a fake Gemini key, save, click activate-candidat-btn, fill message-input, click send-btn. Expect (a) console 400 from generativelanguage.googleapis.com, (b) toast 'Gemini indisponible — bascule automatique sur le mode Serveur', (c) a full CANDIDAT answer appearing from the backend /api/generate stream, (d) mode-badge remains CANDIDAT.
rca of the issue: User reported (per truncated statement): with a fake Gemini key, the fallback to Serveur was not triggering. Verified in this run that streamMessage in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js DOES fall back correctly: (1) streamGemini throws `Gemini 400 — ...` synchronously before any delta, (2) the catch block checks `!emitted && err.name !== 'AbortError'` — both true, (3) handlers.onFallback fires, (4) streamServer is invoked with the same systemMessage/turnMessage and streams the real answer. Fix is already in place and functional.
